sections.normalized_html:
We are told that the width is [MATH: a] feet, and the length is [MATH: 8] feet less than that, so the length is [MATH: a - 8.]

The formula for the perimeter of a rectangle is [MATH: \text{Perimeter} = 2(\text{length}) + 2(\text{width}).]

Substituting the expressions gives [MATH: 2(a - 8) + 2(a).]

Now we simplify: [MATH: 2(a − 8) + 2a|= 2a − 16 + 2a; = 4a − 16]

So, the expression for the perimeter is [MATH: 4a - 16] feet.

The total perimeter of all the frames and trays is [MATH: 476.] Determine the equation representing this situation.

sections.normalized_html:
To model this situation, we will add together the perimeters of all the shapes.

  • Each regular octagon has [MATH: 8] sides of length [MATH: x], so its perimeter is [MATH: 8x.]
    With [MATH: 7] octagons, the total perimeter from the frames is [MATH: 7 \cdot 8x = 56x.]

  • Each rectangle has perimeter [MATH: 2(\text{length} + \text{width}) = 2(4y + y) = 10y.]
    With [MATH: 3] trays, the total perimeter from the rectangles is [MATH: 3 \cdot 10y = 30y.]

Adding both contributions together, we get the total perimeter: [MATH: 56x + 30y = 476]

Thus, the correct equation is [MATH: 56x + 30y = 476.]

sections.normalized_html: The function [MATH: m(x) = 2x + 1{,}200] gives the perimeter, in millimeters ([MATH: \text{mm}]), of an isosceles triangle with two equal sides of length [MATH: x] mm and a fixed base. What is the length of the base of the triangle?
sections.readable_text: The function [MATH: m(x) = 2x + 1{,}200] gives the perimeter, in millimeters ([MATH: \text{mm}]), of an isosceles triangle with two equal sides of length [MATH: x] mm and a fixed base. What is the length of the base of the triangle?

sections.normalized_html:
For an isosceles triangle with two equal sides of length [MATH: x\text{ mm}] and a base of length [MATH: b\text{ mm}], the perimeter is given by

[MATH: P = x + x + b = 2x + b.]

From the problem, we know the perimeter function is

[MATH: m(x) = 2x + 1{,}200.]

By comparing, we get

[MATH: 2x + b = 2x + 1{,}200.]

Therefore, after subtracting [MATH: 2x] from both sides, the length of the base of the triangle is

[MATH: b = 2x + 1{,}200 - 2x = 1{,}200 \text{ mm}.]

Item 2 — Example: Modeling Perimeter Problems Using One-Variable Equations

Example Prompt:

Content:
EXPLANATION

Explanation:
We are told that the width is [MATH: a] feet, and the length is [MATH: 8] feet less than that, so the length is [MATH: a - 8.]

[MATH: \text{Perimeter} = 2(\text{length}) + 2(\text{width}).]

Substituting the expressions gives
[MATH: 2(a - 8) + 2(a).]

Now we simplify:
[MATH: 2(a − 8) + 2a|= 2a − 16 + 2a; = 4a − 16]

So, the expression for the perimeter is [MATH: 4a - 16] feet.

The function [MATH: m(x) = 2x + 1{,}200] gives the perimeter, in millimeters ([MATH: \text{mm}]), of an isosceles triangle with two equal sides of length [MATH: x] mm and a fixed base. What is the length of the base of the triangle?

Content:
EXPLANATION

Explanation:
For an isosceles triangle with two equal sides of length [MATH: x\text{ mm}] and a base of length [MATH: b\text{ mm}], the perimeter is given by

[MATH: P = x + x + b = 2x + b.]

From the problem, we know the perimeter function is

[MATH: m(x) = 2x + 1{,}200.]

By comparing, we get

[MATH: 2x + b = 2x + 1{,}200.]

Therefore, after subtracting [MATH: 2x] from both sides, the length of the base of the triangle is

[MATH: b = 2x + 1{,}200 - 2x = 1{,}200 \text{ mm}.]
